title: Pork Loin with Mustard and Herbs
subtitle: Oven-roasted pork with a mustard and honey crust
excerpt: A quick mustard and honey crust seals in the juices and gives the pork a slightly caramelised outside. Rest it before slicing so the meat stays moist.
sourceNotes: Standard British roast pork loin approach. Mustard and honey is a pairing that works particularly well with lean pork cuts.

content.text: Sear the pork in a hot pan before roasting for better colour all over. The internal temperature is 63 degrees C for safe and juicy pork.
Heat the oven to 200 degrees C. Mix the mustard, honey, garlic, rosemary, lemon zest, and lemon juice in a small bowl.
Season the pork all over. Heat the olive oil in an ovenproof frying pan or roasting tin over high heat. Sear the pork for 2 minutes on each side.
Spread the mustard mixture over the top and sides of the pork.
Transfer to the oven. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes until the internal temperature reads 63 degrees C.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing into rounds.

items.symptom: Mustard crust burnt before meat is cooked through.
items.cause: Oven too hot or the honey caramelised quickly.
items.fix: Tent with foil and continue roasting; remove foil for last 5 minutes.

items.cause: Overcooked past 68 degrees C or rested too briefly.
items.fix: Use a probe and pull at 63 degrees C; rest a full 10 minutes.

items.symptom: No colour on the outside after searing.
items.cause: Pan was not hot enough or meat was wet.
items.fix: Pat dry before searing; make sure the pan is smoking before adding pork.
